title: Patel Retail Ltd - 544487 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Patel Retail Q4 FY26 PAT rose 39.07% YoY to INR9.98 crore on 53.35% higher income, but EBITDA margin fell to 6.70% as new-store costs hit.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 total income rose 53.35% YoY to INR339.55 crore, with EBITDA up 31.21% to INR22.74 crore and PAT up 39.07% to INR9.98 crore. FY26 total income crossed INR1,000 crore at INR1,059.29 crore (+28.25%), with PAT up 54.48% to INR39.05 crore and PAT margin at 3.69%. Management attributed the weak Q4 EBITDA margin to upfront costs of new stores and said revenue ramp-up would come in FY27. Analyst questions focused on falling same-store sales (~5%), gross margin compression, a sizeable other-income (FX gain) contribution, and inventory and receivables build-up; several answers were incomplete or inconsistent.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: 51 stores after Rasayani opening in April 2026 (over 2.29 lakh sq ft); 50th store at Thakurli in Q4. Retail sales INR429 crore in FY26; management cited retail EBITDA margin of 7-8% and gross margin of 14-15%, and retail contributes about 35-38% of PAT excluding other income.

segments.name: Manufacturing and processing (B2B)
segments.commentary: Ambernath and Kutch capacity over 1.47 lakh MTPA; utilisation 50-55% vs 45-48% earlier. Management cited about INR618 crore manufacturing and processing sales in FY26, of which about INR319 crore exports; gross margin guided at 16-17% (FY27: 18-20%). Management put manufacturing EBITDA margin at roughly 6.5-7%.

segments.name: Private label / own brands
segments.commentary: Own brands (Indian Chaska, Patel Fresh, Blue Nation, Patel Essentials) are about 17.5% of retail sales; own brands reportedly carry 30-35% operating margins per management, with non-branded gross margin of 15-16%. Indian Chaska distribution covers six states, with MP and Delhi in progress.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at approximately 8-9%.
Gross margin guided at 15-20% overall; FY27 mix expected at 18-20% for B2B and 15-16% for retail.
Management expects double-digit revenue growth in FY27, with 'higher side' at 20% and above, but declined to disclose numbers formally.
Plans to open 8-10 stores a year, with focus on western suburbs and PCMC; possible Gujarat entry. Management said 52 stores as of the call date and seven or eight more expected in FY27.
Management expects positive operating cash flow by H1 FY27 as inventory normalises.
Management expects PAT margin to increase, and expects manufacturing utilisation to rise.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity at Ambernath and Kutch exceeds 1.47 lakh MTPA; utilisation 50-55%, up 4-5 percentage points.
Retail network 51 stores, over 2.29 lakh sq ft; management carries about INR2,000-2,500 inventory per sq ft at store level.
Distribution centre in the cluster holds an additional INR15-20 crore of inventory per management.
Plans to start whole spices in the month of the call, then seasonings, pastes, snacks, and noodles or pasta depending on distribution.
Automation investment planned to improve productivity and cost efficiency.
demand_pricing: Same-store sales growth around 5%; management said mature stores grow 5-6%, versus analyst's recollection of 8-10%.
Grocery and staples are about 68-70% of retail revenue.
Export order book held at INR50-100 crore per management; current export order book figure not provided on the call.
Exports to Sri Lanka, Middle East, Europe, US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, with African markets being pursued; management says 35+ countries.
Other income of about INR5 crore in Q4 is mainly FX gain on export receivables; management said INR8-9 crore per year is typical and expected to keep rising.
Management said commodity prices have peaked and are declining, and expects inventory gains from raw material procured at competitive prices.

qa_highlights.question: Why did same-store sales appear to slow from 8-10% to about 5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 5% is good for mature stores, cited no specific reason, and said most revenue comes from grocery and staples (68-70%).

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory and working capital rise so much?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said incremental working capital was funded from IPO proceeds (INR115 crore deployed into working capital). Management also cited export order book, transit times, and mixed shipments; the exact export order book was not disclosed on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 margin decline and gross margin fall from about 20% to 14.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed Q4 margin pressure to upfront costs of new stores, and said it is temporary. He did not separately quantify the gross margin decline; management said the West Asia situation had not been the primary factor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the other income and is it recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said other income is mainly FX gain on export receivables, about INR8-9 crore a year, and expected to keep rising. Management did not explain why the Q4 figure was about INR5 crore or why the gain would be recurring.

qa_highlights.question: Why is retail inventory at about INR90 crore, above the INR55-58 crore implied by store-level inventory per sq ft?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the difference reflects a cluster distribution centre (INR15-20 crore) and category-level inventory days, including about three months of spices stock and three to four months for plastic and steel, with festive stock also included.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise from INR125 crore to INR161-162 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about 90% of receivables are less than six months old. He did not explain the increase.

risks_watch: Same-store sales growth of about 5% versus the 8-10% the analyst cited previously; management did not give a clear reason for the slowdown.
Gross margin fell sharply in Q4 (analyst cited about 14.5% versus about 20% a year earlier); management has not quantified the cause.
Other income (FX gain) of about INR5 crore in Q4 is a large share of PAT growth; the analyst argued that excluding it would show a decline.
Inventory (INR259-260 crore) and receivables (INR161-162 crore) rose sharply; management guided to positive operating cash flow only by H1 FY27.
Middle East and West Asia disruption may hit export volumes; management said it is pushing domestic sales to compensate.
DGFT wheat flour export scheme is policy-dependent; management said it does not rely on it fully.
Several Q&A answers were inconsistent or incomplete, including the export order book, the margin split between B2B and B2C, and the retail gross margin figures.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and capacity plans, with management repeatedly calling Q4 margin dip temporary. Evasive on specifics: declined to give the export order book, FY27 revenue numbers, and the cause of the gross margin fall, and several answers were contradictory on margin and sales-mix figures.
key_quotes: So, in Q4, we have incurred the initial cost and the revenue is likely to be generated into fiscal '26-'27.
We have already achieved the debt-equity ratio to 0.34 from 1.34 in the fiscal '26.
Hitesh Sawlani: Higher side double-digit growth, you can say 20% and above.
We don't want to dump our goods and go wide and deep.

adds.what: Retail store additions: 8-10 stores per year, 7-8 more expected in FY27 (western suburbs, PCMC, possible Gujarat)
Whole spices production line to start in the month of the call, then seasonings, pastes, snacks, noodles/pasta
Automation investment to improve productivity and cost efficiency (no size or timing given)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 20% and above (higher double-digit) and EBITDA margin of 8-9%, backed by 8-10 new stores a year, a whole-spices line starting now, and manufacturing utilisation at 50-55% rising; but no firm order or contract numbers, and same-store sales slowed to about 5%, so backing is partial.
